content.thinking:
I need to write the whole scene in one pass to conserve calls, so I'm planning the desert oasis layout: a sand dune disc, a pond, swept palm leaves, lathe-built tents, capsule-rod camels, rocks, crates, and a campfire, pulling in the builder, paint, texture, and rng utilities.

I'm working out the API details for lathes, extrudes, sweeps, rods, capsules, and spikes, deciding the base will be a sandy disc about 1.3m radius with sunken dune lumps, topped by a slightly raised water-colored pond with stone rim, and palms standing roughly 1.5m tall within a diorama spanning around 2.6 meters.

For scaling the scene elements, I'm settling on camels around 0.5m tall, palms about 1.3m, and tents around 0.5m. I'm designing a local-to-world coordinate helper that rotates by yaw and translates points, then building the camel's body as a capsule shape using this helper rather than scaled spheres, since scaling conflicts with the rotation frame.

Still defining camel geometry...

For the painting, I'll apply stripes along z for the blanket, mottled texture for sand, and striped fabric for the tent, with the palm trunk getting subtle banded scale texture using stripes along y. Then I'm planning the palm fronds as drooping swept shapes arranged around the crown.

I should compute a proper perpendicular vector for the leaf's orientation rather than assuming the up axis works directly, using a cross product against the frond's side direction. For the leaf shape itself, I'm defining a pointed outline with tapered points along a 0.36 length, fitting onto 0.7-long fronds against a 1.2-unit trunk.

Now I'm adding a gradient paint for the leaf, mixing dark to light green based on position along its length, plus coconuts and date clusters under the crown. For the tents, I'm building a lathe-based cone shape with a spinning outline and striped paint based on angle around the axis.

Positioning the door against the lower vertical wall of the tent, approximating the polygon's apothem with enough segments to get a near-circular cross-section, then placing the door triangle just outside that radius.

I'm shaping the door as an arched outline and orienting it to face toward the pond, using a horizontal perpendicular vector for the thickness axis so it extrudes correctly. Now moving on to building the second, larger tent.

For Tent B, I'm designing a Bedouin-style ridge tent with a sagging A-frame profile extruded into a solid prism, adding a front awning and vertical stripe texturing along the gable faces, plus support poles.

Now I'm adding the dark gable triangle at the opening, some rug accents, and a pond feature using a flat cylinder disk with a mottled teal water texture and a rim of small scattered stones, positioned near the layout's sandy base.

Working out the layout coordinates: pond centered with a small radius, palms placed around it at varying sizes and leans, two tents positioned at wider radius with doors facing the pond, and camels placed nearby—one standing and oriented toward the pond, one kneeling with a simplified folded-leg lower body.

I'm placing the campfire near tent A, repositioning the palms to avoid overlap, and planning additional details like cacti, rocks, dune lumps, crates, a skull on a dune, and reeds and lilies around the pond for atmosphere.

Still working out dune placement so the lumps stay within the base disc radius without extending past its edges.

I'm also planning a darker rim band around the base using a lathe profile, plus mottled sand-colored paint and ripple stripe textures for the surface detail.

Still writing sand shader colors...

Now I'm planning the camel's physical features: dark hooves, a tufted tail rod, whimsical oversized eyes with white highlights, blushing pink cheeks, and a gold bell with strap and tassels on the neck. I'm sketching out body dimensions too—the torso as a capsule shape with a chest sphere attached.

Working out the hump placement and the leg geometry next, figuring out hip, knee, and hoof positions relative to the ground for each limb.

Still building the head and neck geometry... I'm planning the head with capsule neck-to-skull, a muzzle sphere with nostrils, small spike ears, and eyes positioned symmetrically. For the kneeling pose variant, I'm thinking of lowering the body and folding the legs horizontally underneath while keeping the neck upright.

Now I'm sketching out a single camel-building function that takes position, yaw, and kneeling/blanket options, working out the folded leg geometry as rods resting on the ground for both front and rear legs, and adjusting the neck's vertical offset to match the lowered kneeling body.

For loading up the kneeling camel, I'm thinking through packs like sack spheres and rolled rugs, plus a draped saddle blanket for the standing one made of angled thin boxes along the hump, considering whether I need a frustum-box helper to get the draping shape right.

Working out the extrude direction for the blanket outline relative to the camel's yaw, and now sketching the front-view points that trace the drape curve down each side of the hump.

Actually I can simplify by just drawing the blanket as a solid octagon band wrapped around the body near the hump, since the interior stays hidden inside the body anyway — a simple octagon extrusion with modest thickness should read fine visually.

Still refining the blanket outline...

For the stripe pattern, I'm computing stripes based on y-coordinate in meters, alternating color bands every 0.035 units, applying it to both the body and walls.

Now I'm planning more scene detail: gold tassels at the flap corners, then moving to Tent B's roof stripes, a flag-topped ridge pole, guy ropes and pegs, plus rugs, cushions, lathe-turned pottery vases, crates, a barrel, a campfire with log rods and glowing orange flame spikes, a cooking pot, a ring of stones, and a cactus.

For the cactus I'm adding pink flower spheres, and I'm deciding to skip a skull prop in favor of bleached bones or a signpost with an arrow extrude instead. I'm sketching whimsical touches like star lanterns glowing on the palm, a tiny fish capsule in the pond, lily pads with pink flowers, and reeds scattered around the pond using a frame import I need to pull in from the source module -- accepting some risk that it's exported correctly, with cards as a fallback if not.

Switching to safer thin cone spikes for reeds instead of cards to avoid import risk, and reusing an SVG diamond-pattern texture on thin box geometry for rugs so I only need to generate one pattern for two rugs. Now I'm tallying up the total part count across four palm trees with their trunks, rings, and fronds to make sure I stay well under the limit.

Keeping extrusions cheap with no smoothing or bevel, and limiting the overall color palette to around 40 flat tones. I'm sketching out a reusable palm-generation function that takes position, height, lean direction, and scale, using a catmull curve for the trunk path with tapered radius, a bulging base, striped rings, and a crown of nine long fronds plus four shorter upright ones.

Still defining frond geometry...

Still writing frond outline code...

I also want to add a few coconuts as small brown spheres near the trunk top, and a striped tent in the composition.

Thinking about adding a glow lantern — simplest to hang it from the tent's front pole rather than complicate the palm, avoiding position conflicts. Now starting the actual build script, setting up imports for the builder, path, paint utilities, rng, texture, and glow kit, plus defining metadata and a grain constant before writing the build function.

Setting up helper functions for vectors, sphere geometry, and ball placement, working through type compatibility for color/fill parameters between Paint and ColorInput types.

Writing box helper function...

Now I'm working out the camel's local coordinate frame, computing local-to-world positions based on yaw rotation, and figuring out how to orient the camel to face toward the pond using atan2.

Still shaping camel geometry...

Adding cheek blush, spiked ears, and brow tuft, then working out mane spikes along the neck by sampling points on the neck's curved path and angling each spike tip backward and upward from its base.

Now I'm building the legs: front legs as tapered rod segments from hip to knee to hoof, with a ball joint at the knee and a dark box-shaped hoof rotated to match leg yaw.

Still placing leg joints and hooves...

Now I'm sketching the tail as a sweep from the hip down to a dark tuft ball, checking it works with the kneeling offset, then laying out the blanket geometry with its hump and thickness centered on the body.

Working out the blanket outline height against the hump and body surface so the hump pokes out above the blanket without being swallowed by the body capsule, adjusting the top arc points for the outline shape.

Now I'm placing tassel balls along the blanket edge and sketching the hanging sacks and packs for the kneeling camel pose, positioning them at the sides near the hump.

For the standing camel I'm adding a cross-rod over the hump and a rolled rug on the rear with cream-tipped ends, then considering a whimsical touch like a tiny flower garland on the head instead of a saddle cushion.

I'll add a small beaded garland loop around the camel's neck using five pink/orange balls, taper the trunk with a smoothly narrowing sweep radius, and generate ten fronds swept around the top using leaf vectors for droop.

Writing frond geometry...

Leaves extrude with thickness along the up-slope and side axes, so ribs get skipped since the leaf shape already covers them, but I'll add a rib detail for extra color. Dates cluster as orange balls under the crown. For tents, I'm sketching a conical whimsical tent shape as a lathe profile with a flared skirt base, considering whether to layer a second lighter cone roof overlay.

Adding stripe decoration, pole spike, and pennant flag...

Now I'm adding a gold trim ring around the wall top using a closed catmull path, with a helper function to generate ring points at a given radius and height.

For the flap door, I'm making it a darker purple-gray with a slightly larger gold frame behind it for contrast.

For tent B, a ridge tent, I'm figuring out orientation—it needs to face the pond, so I'm calculating the yaw angle from its position relative to the pond center, then writing a generic local coordinate function so the tent can be built with its ridge along a rotated local axis rather than assuming world alignment.

Now I'm building the tent body as a large extruded prism following a pentagon-ish front profile, adding vertical gable stripes alternating red and cream based on position along the width, and shaping a thin sloped awning canopy out front using a wedge-shaped side-view outline.

Confirming the local-x derivation checks out, so I'll use one shared paint helper for both stripe sections. Then I'm adding the front support rods at the canopy corners and extruding an arched doorway outline on the gable front as a thin dark panel.

Adding tied flaps, flag poles at the gable corners, a textured rug box, squashed cushion shapes, and barrel/crate props out front. Then I'm laying out the guy-rope rods running from the eaves down to ground pegs for both tents.

Now I'm placing the campfire near tent A: a ring of gray stone balls, crossing log rods, flame spikes in orange and yellow with ember glow, plus a kettle resting on a flat stone beside the fire.

I'm adding more props: terracotta vases near tent B, crates with striped lids and rope, a hooped barrel, sacks, two cacti with capsule trunks and pink flower balls, a rock cluster, and the start of palm trees.

Now I'm placing several palm trees around the pond with varying heights and lean angles so their crowns arch over the water, plus a smaller young palm near where the camels will go.

I'm checking tent B's rug position against the forward direction from its yaw angle, noticing it lands too close to palm P2, so I'm nudging P2's position slightly to clear the collision.

I'm now checking tent B's distance from center — its rotated corners extend past the 1.4 boundary, so I'm pulling the whole tent inward toward (0.72,-0.62) and recomputing the rear corner distances to confirm it now fits within bounds.

Next I compute the tent's facing yaw toward the pond center and check the rug's placement — it ends up sitting right on the pond's rim, so I shrink the rug distance and nudge the pond center slightly to resolve the overlap, then recheck the rug's distance from the adjusted pond center.

I also verify the second palm tree's distance from both the pond and the rug to confirm there's no overlap with its trunk radius, then move to tent A, calculating its distance and facing yaw toward the pond and positioning its door accordingly. Finally I place the campfire in front-right of tent A and start positioning jars and crates near tent B's left side.

Checking a cactus placement near tent A for distance conflicts, then verifying rocks and dune lumps near tent B stay within bounds by computing their ellipse extents against the center radius.

Adjusting the dune sink depth so it stays within a small percentage of model height, then working out the pond geometry with a sunken water disc and a raised sand rim built from a lathe annulus.

Adding stones around the rim, reeds on one side, lily pads with little pink flowers, and a whimsical touch: a fish mid-leap above the pond made from a tilted orange capsule with a tail and fin.

I'm also adding a splash ring at the water surface, and considering a small signpost near the tent with an "OASIS" text decal, deciding the floating fish is fine as a playful disconnected detail.

Rather than SVG text (risk of font rasterization issues), I'll use shape-based icons instead -- a palm+wave plaque on a round sign board. Now I'm checking type imports for Paint and OutlinePoint before writing the actual code.

Setting up color type definitions...

Writing sphere geometry and ball helper functions...

Defining the sand paint texture...

Working through the base lathe shape with sand coloring, plus a slightly darker rim band to avoid z-fighting at the overlapping inner edges.

Writing helper functions for flags and local transforms...

I'm adding a scalloped triangle valance along the awning edge with alternating red and cream colors, while keeping the other tent's trim simpler, and sketching out palm frond counts before finalizing the scene.

Now I'm defining a pennant flag shape and adding slight random variance to palm frond angles for a more natural look, then moving into the full code with careful attention to variable types. I'm also wiring up glowing effects for the flame spikes, embers, and lanterns, and figuring out how to hang lanterns from the tent poles using a rod from the pole top.
